target_customer: Researchers, clinical labs, public health agencies, and biotech and food safety teams doing microbial sequencing
problem: Identifying microbes in sequencing data was slow and clunky. One Codex built a fast search of a large microbial reference database that identifies genomic datasets in minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS data platform plus sequencing services

founders.name: Nick Greenfield
founders.background_notes: YC blog calls him a former data scientist; his YC profile calls him a former management consultant who moved into software, data and biology. Later VP of Product and Tech (Biosecurity) at Ginkgo Bioworks 2022 to 2023.

founders.name: Nik Krumm
education: University of Washington, PhD in Genome Sciences

competitors.name: Kraken
competitors.what: Open source k-mer based metagenomic classifier, the main free alternative

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time search across about 30,000 reference genomes at millions of base pairs per second needed novel indexing plus bioinformatics curation of the reference database.

defensibility.rationale: A curated, growing reference database and workflow integrations raised switching costs, but open source tools like Kraken offered a free substitute.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Illumina exposed third-party analysis apps on BaseSpace and One Codex integrated with it rather than being copied. A diagnostics company, Invitae, bought One Codex in February 2021 and sold it back to employees in September 2022.

market_need_then: Sequencing costs were falling and researchers, clinicians and public health officials had sequenced over 100,000 genomes by 2014, but analysis tools were slow and hard to use per the YC blog.

branding.domain_note: Uses onecodex.com; the legal entity was Reference Genomics, Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as a Google for genomic data.

branding.community_and_virality: Won a CDC prize for catching bad E. coli according to Xconomy listing; not opened.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within bioinformatics and cited in a 2015 preprint, with a trademark registered in 2019, but little consumer or press brand activity found.

outcome_analysis: One Codex built a fast microbial genomics data platform from a YC Summer 2014 start and was acquired by the diagnostics company Invitae in February 2021. Invitae sold its equity back for an immaterial amount in September 2022 in an employee buyout, so the company continues independently in biosecurity, food safety and microbiome work. The acquisition price is not reliably public, and funding beyond YC could not be verified.
notes: Unverified: CB Insights shows a seed round dated April 2015 with investors including DCVC, Mount Pleasant and Healthy Ventures, but amounts conflict across aggregators, so no round is recorded. A Dealroom profile gives an 83.4 million dollar acquisition price, seen in one place only, so amount_usd is null. Spin-out in September 2022 is described by Invitae filing language in a search snippet and by the YC page. Kraken source is a snippet of One Codex docs, not opened; CosmosID is listed as a competitor by CB Insights without dates. Founder education for Greenfield not found. Completeness pass: the seed round is recorded from CB Insights (April 2015) with amount null because amounts conflict (CB Insights $20K total, Caplight $320K total with a May 2015 seed date, Craft $120K). Bio-IT World (Feb 2015) mentions a private financing from undisclosed investors. The round rests on a single database; investors DCVC and Mount Pleasant come from CB Insights investor listings.
